rationale: C07 and C17 are the closest candidates because they concern courts-martial and contain transitional rules for pending proceedings and prior offenses. They do not, however, supply the child's distinctive petition-and-remedy machinery: eligibility and deadlines for petitions, a good-cause/injustice standard, required petition contents, investigation and hearing authority, written disposition, or procedures following the grant of a new trial. C18 contains detailed procedural regulations for disciplinary boards, but its administrative investigation framework is materially different from the child's post-conviction military-review process. Any overlap is attributable to broad military-justice subject matter or generic adjudicative procedure rather than a concrete drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The new trial shall be on the same charges and specifications originally preferred against the accused...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C07: "This manual shall be in force and effect in the Army of the United States... with respect to all court-martial processes..."
shared_material.explanation: Both concern court-martial proceedings, but the parent provides only an effective-date and transition rule, not the child's new-trial procedure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The petition may be submitted either by the accused or by his representative...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C18: "Notice of charges; right to counsel" and detailed procedures for boards of investigation.
shared_material.explanation: Both regulate procedural rights in disciplinary matters, but C18 lacks the petition, post-conviction review, good-cause standard, and remedial sequence central to the child.
